claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The target samples may contain defects or impurities, including approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
A machine-learning approach can predict the thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed approach can distinguish lattice and electronic contributions to thermal conductivity.
The proposed approach will outperform earlier analytical approaches.
Improved performance will result from learning relationships among alloy composition, structure, and thermal properties.
The machine-learning algorithm will capture atomic-scale complexity not adequately represented by earlier approaches.
The expected predictive improvement is 10–20% relative to earlier approaches.
The relevant measured total thermal-conductivity baseline is 10–17 W/(K m) from 300 to 1200 K.
The proposed approach is intended to apply below 200 K and from 300 to 1200 K.
Temperatures below 200 K and above 1200 K are stated as applicability limits.
Highly defective or highly impure samples are outside the stated sample applicability limits.
Predictions are especially uncertain below 50 K, above 1500 K, and for samples with high defect or impurity concentrations.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing predictions with measurements below 200 K and above 1000 K across samples having different defect and impurity concentrations.
Deviation from experiment by more than 20% at multiple temperatures or for multiple sample types would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions include temperatures below 200 K within the intended application range, while the boundary simultaneously identifies temperatures below 200 K as an applicability limit.

The boundary places the upper applicability limit above 1200 K, whereas uncertainty is only specifically emphasized above 1500 K, leaving the status of predictions from 1200 to 1500 K inconsistent or unclear.
